rationale: All three acceptance criteria pass. One major finding (CR-001): the pulse-ring animation <div> inside the button is not marked aria-hidden="true". The diff correctly added aria-hidden to both SVG icons but missed this decorative element, leaving it inconsistent. While aria-label on the parent button overrides accessible-name computation in most screen readers, adding aria-hidden to the div is consistent with the approach used for the sibling SVGs and eliminates any residual AT noise. The fix is a one-liner. Three pre-existing issues are deferred (optimistic mic state before getUserMedia resolves, double-activation window during the async call, no aria-live for auto-stop after timeout) — all predate this diff and are out of scope for this accessibility ticket. 2 dismissed; 3 deferred.

business_review.criterion: The 'Use voice' button has an accessible name: 'Use voice'
business_review.notes: aria-label='Use voice' when isUserSpeaking is false; confirmed by test getByRole('button', { name: 'Use voice' }).

business_review.criterion: After activation, the screen reader announces 'Stop listening'
business_review.notes: aria-label switches to 'Stop listening' when isUserSpeaking is true; confirmed by test findByRole('button', { name: 'Stop listening' }).

business_review.criterion: SVG icons inside the button are hidden from assistive technology
business_review.notes: Both StopSvg and RecordSvg receive aria-hidden="true", preventing double-announcement alongside the button label.

standards_review.notes: Commit subject 'EPMCDME-8444: Add accessible name to voice recorder button' follows the ticket-prefix convention.
aria-label on icon button and aria-hidden on decorative SVGs are correct per guide. Pulse-ring div is missing aria-hidden (see CR-001).
No security-relevant changes in this diff.

findings.problem: The pulse-ring animation <div> rendered inside the button when isUserSpeaking is true is not aria-hidden. The diff added aria-hidden to both SVG icons but missed this decorative element.
findings.impact: Some AT may traverse the button's accessible subtree despite the explicit aria-label, announcing an unlabelled child element or producing an extra pause. Inconsistent with the aria-hidden treatment applied to the sibling SVG icons in the same change.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-hidden="true" to the pulse-ring div: <div aria-hidden="true" className="absolute left-0 border-4 border-text-accent rounded-full pulse-ring bg-transparent size-[30px]" />
